Definition: from G1537 and G2476; to put (stand) out of wits, i.e. astound, or (reflexively) become astounded, insane:--amaze, be (make) astonished, be beside self (selves), bewitch, wonder.
BiblicalUsage: exístēmi means amaze, be (make) astonished, be beside self (selves), bewitch, wonder. In Matthew 12:23, the text says "And all the people were amazed." In Mark 2:12, the text says "insomuch that they were all amazed."
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that exístēmi matters because miracles are not magic tricks; they are God showing His hand in the open. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
RelatedEvents: Pentecost; The Birth of Jesus; The Tower of Babel
